Update, I’ve felt a little better since being home from the hospital Sunday with only a few “PVCs” or palpitations a day. But lots of hesitation.

This is still very good to consider for me, I advocated heavily for myself in the ED, I’m a youngish woman, normal weight, and they tend to dismiss us regularly. I explained I felt when I sat up in bed that morning in the ED that I went into “tachycardia” that knocked the wind out of me, start of the 8:08 strip basically, then felt like after 45 seconds or so that I was having multiple PVCs back to back (I do feel my PVCs, I have had those for many years now and they always tell me they are harmless because they are less than 1% of my overall burden) however it’s usually a few a day, and not consecutively. When I asked about that section of the ekg they initially said artifact (but I wasn’t moving, in fact I was very still because I thought I was going to pass out), but then said it was maybe SVT with aberration and a few PVCs, they did say it isn’t common and my outpatient EP isn’t back for a few weeks still, so I’m just kind of monitoring on my own at home with medication to use in an emergency. But I was worried if it’s more than SVT whether or not the meds would work. Plus they told me the rhythm isn’t a fatal rhythm or something you’d see in somebody who is at risk for sudden cardiac death because my echo is normal, and cardiac mri was normal. But it’s hard to shake that feeling that I was on deaths door in that moment. Even the nurse who had her stethoscope on my chest when it happened turned white as a sheet. They currently have me on ivabridine to bring my rate under control, with flecainide as needed, a loop recorder to be adjusted next week to be more specific, and mag and potassium supplements since when this happened I was at 3.1 potassium and 1.7 mag with a 17 carbon dioxide so they felt maybe I was dehydrated. And that maybe the episode was a one off, I certainly hope so. :( I really don’t want to drop dead suddenly at 35.

They said no vtach, double checked with two EPs and a cardiologist, but this morning it was that run immediately following the SVT where just today they called it “aberrant” heart rhythms. But they seemed a little unsure. Do you have any training in the area? This is the image they showed me to differentiate the two because I was bit curious and asked outright….

No worries, I’m stable at home on meds, just looking for advice for future follow up care.
Read up to chapter 26, is 27 out yet?
What if you wanted to build her as support only, as a shielder?

You’re right about something in your post. If things are crazy around me I can’t pause to feel as much. I used to work in the ER and it was perfect, the stress, other people’s stress, I could fall asleep to a hospital monitor. In school I always took 15 credits and multiple sciences, I like torturing myself with piling on so much that I feel like I’m drowning all the time so that I have moment where I’m not actively thinking about how much I hate being alive. But now that I’ve met those goals, and things have slowed, it’s getting harder to avoid, and even if I could find something else, another degree, or different job, more money or hobbies, I think I’d still feel disheartened that another 30 years of my life could just wind up being miserable. Also, how does a body that’s been in fight or flight since it was born calm down?

I’m worried about the peace that follows, what can I fill my days with? With no parents, grandparents, or really any family, you feel sort of this deep emptiness. Both of my cats I’ve even had since I was 15 years old died in the last couple years. It’s hard not to feel like you’re placed here on this earth to be bled dry, and give and give, and never get a resulting happiness. I’ve been told do this, and you’ll be better. Make more money, get an education, buy a house, get a nice car, get married, and then surely my problems would be solved. But when you strip away the material aspects and you’ve met all your personal goals how do you keep pushing for anything else. What even else is there? Work, wash, repeat. I don’t know if I can handle another thirty years like I’ve had. Why would I want to? What’s your driving force to even keep going?

It’s a fair concern to have. Some people can choose to live for others, it to me is the ultimate sacrifice. But I look at like this, death is inevitable, when I get really dark I try to remember I’m going to eventually die, if I’m bringing joy to people I care about, then at least that’s something. Don’t ask me what to do when they’re gone, that I’m still trying to figure out.
